evidence.text: The printed 不 entry calls 不 a pictograph and reports the calyx/stalk analysis: it cites 《甲骨文字典》 for 不 as an original graph for 柎, glossed as the base of a flower receptacle, and quotes the 《詩·小雅·棠棣》 gloss with Zheng Xuan’s note that 不 should be 柎 and that 不 and 柎 were homophonous in ancient pronunciation. It then characterizes the Shuowen explanation as inaccurate and describes borrowing 不 for negation before verbs and adjectives. The scan shows printed headword 不 and the cited quotation; I directly inspected the pixels for the entry and the continuation on the next page.

evidence.source: 周堯, 「『不』字本義為花梢說質疑」
evidence.text: Zhou reviews the flower-calyx account and challenges it against oracle-bone shapes, noting forms that the account does not explain. He entertains a plant-root possibility from graphic comparison, but says that ancient texts do not use 不 with a root meaning and leaves the original sense unresolved. This cautions against presenting the calyx account or the proposed root link as settled.
evidence.title: 「『不』字本義為花梢說質疑」

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Character Database, CUHK)
evidence.field: 形義源流通解; oracle-bone and bronze uses
evidence.text: The entry reports two analyses: a ground line with root-like strokes, with Chen Shihui identifying 不 as an original graph for 茇, and a flower-receptacle/calyx analysis identifying 不 as an original graph for 柎. It separately quotes Shuowen’s bird-flying-upward explanation. The database reports oracle-bone negative-adverb use and names, and bronze uses including negation and readings/uses as 丕 ‘great’ and 邳. These are reported interpretations and lexicographic examples, not a settled origin or a full semantic chronology.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 漢字甲骨部件分析：不

evidence.text: The authors place 不 as a general negative marker in oracle-bone inscriptions broadly dated to the 14th–11th centuries BCE. They cite 王不往于田 (‘the king will not go hunting’) and note competing hypotheses about how 不 and 弗 differ in oracle-bone use. This documents use of the negative word, not the graph’s pictured origin.
evidence.title: A Typological Study of Negation in Sinitic Languages: Synchronic and Diachronic Views

evidence.text: The database presents 不 as the original form of 胚 and interprets the horizontal stroke as ground and the lower strokes as germinating-seed roots. It also reports the calyx explanation and borrowing for negation. It lists oracle, bronze, Chu manuscript, small-seal, and Shuowen stages without textually dating each form. These are database-reported analyses, not a dated chain of semantic development.
evidence.title: 漢字「不」：字形演變

evidence.source: Park Hyun Joo (박현주), ‘不’字의 원형과 선진시기 의미 변화 고찰
evidence.text: The accessible abstract proposes a distinct account: 不 imitates the tassel at the rear of a particular graph for 戈, with a sound relationship to a tassel word. The abstract supplies incomplete glyph characters for the proposed weapon variant, so its precise identity and full argument cannot be confirmed from this record. This is an attributed proposal, not corroboration for the calyx or root explanations.
evidence.title: ‘不’字의 원형과 선진시기 의미 변화 고찰

The locally inspected 《字源》 passage supports an attributed calyx/柎 analysis, but not its truth. The original referent and proposed semantic route to negation remain unresolved; the book entry ends partway through its account and the continuation is on PDF page 1051.

Zhou’s article questions the calyx interpretation and leaves a root-related account unresolved. No earliest attestation for a literal calyx, plant root, or bird sense, nor a dated transition from such a sense to negation, was established.

The accessible KCI abstract proposes 不 as resembling a tassel part of a戈-related graph and argues for a sound connection to a tassel word. Its missing glyph strings prevent precise identification of the proposed graph in this abstract; the full article was not accessed.
The broad 14th–11th-century BCE dating of oracle-bone negative use does not provide a specific date for any one 不 occurrence. No primary artifact image for the cited example was inspected.

No local structured Baxter–Sagart row applies because no phonetic component is supported. Current Mandarin local row provided for 不 is bù; its requested Unicode Unihan codepoint page returned an internal error, so no upstream click-through confirmation is included.
No actual distinct phonetic component is supported in the inspected paleographic accounts. Whole-graph loan proposals are separate from a component-to-host phonetic analysis.
